title: Choose the learning experience direction
question: Every option keeps the book theme and puts older learners first. Choose a direction, ask for a fresh hand, or take the category standard.

options.label: The Living Folio
options.lineage: Split-flap departure boards, translated into a bookish study folio
options.thesis: A familiar study workspace where one calm folio marker advances as learners move through a lesson.
options.viewport: A standard learner workspace: clear navigation, today's study, a next lesson, and named progress. A brief, restrained folio transition marks meaningful lesson progress.
options.risk: If the folio movement spreads to routine interactions, it will feel theatrical instead of natural.

raised.raise: Colour can distinguish a course, but never replaces its readable name.
Progress always appears as named, understandable milestones before any visual path.
Study sessions remain flexible; no fixed sides or assumed duration.
Course names, progress and next actions align with deliberate editorial precision.
Learning claims sit beside real lesson tasks, not decorative promises.
Motion marks a real learner action only; the interface never pretends to be a live departures board.

options.label: The Annotated Reader
options.lineage: University reading journals and useful marginal notes
options.thesis: A calm, book-first study journal that makes today's work and the next step easy to find.
options.viewport: A clear learner workspace with the current lesson up front, a slim chapter index, and progress notes kept in the margin.
options.risk: Margin details must stay functional, not turn the screen into ruled-paper wallpaper.

options.label: The Chapter Grid
options.thesis: A chapter-led learning workspace where courses, progress and next actions sit in a precise grid.
options.viewport: A familiar learner shell with course modules arranged in a clear grid and the next lesson given priority.
options.case: The grid brings strong course hierarchy and task clarity, but carries less of the requested book identity than the folio directions.
options.risk: An over-visible grid could make the study space feel like a worksheet.

options.label: The Coded Catalog Sleeve
options.thesis: Course identities reduced to a pulse and a coded strip of colour.
options.case: Fuses poorly: replacing course names with a colour code hides the information learners need.
options.kept: A consistent course accent, always paired with a readable title.
options.risk: A cryptic visual code would make navigation harder.

options.label: The Study Atlas
options.thesis: Study progress drawn as a field of connected milestones.
options.case: The map may feel exploratory, but an astronomy metaphor does not explain ordinary lesson states clearly enough.
options.kept: Show named milestones in a legible sequence before adding any path visualization.
options.risk: A decorative map can turn clear progress into a puzzle.

options.label: The Study Mixtape
options.thesis: Study activities grouped into two sides of a timed session.
options.case: The split-side metaphor assumes a fixed session length and imposes structure that conflicts with flexible pacing.
options.kept: Make it easy to return to the next unfinished study step.
options.risk: A side-A/side-B interaction is cute but can obstruct a real task.

options.label: The Claim-and-Proof Page
options.thesis: Each learning claim is paired immediately with a product example.
options.case: This is a sales-page structure, not a daily learning workspace; its neutral, sparse system also weakens active learning states.
options.kept: Pair learning actions with concrete lesson content instead of unsupported promises.
options.risk: Marketing conventions would make the learner app feel like an advertisement.

options.label: The Departure-Board Duplicate
options.thesis: A second reading of the same changing-row metaphor.
options.case: It duplicates the assigned direction without adding student identity or product clarity.
options.kept: Animate only meaningful learner progress; do not imitate live departure data.
options.risk: Repeated flips would compete with reading and accessibility.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A familiar, polished learning dashboard with no distinctive book-world expression.
canonCard.viewport: A conventional course dashboard with clear navigation, progress summaries and a task list.
canonCard.risk: It meets category expectations but gives up the requested book identity.
